To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of de novo software for peptide sequencing is a valuable tool in shotgun proteomics.
the use of different methods of data analysis in shotgun proteomics allows identification of a significant proportion of protein sequences.

the use of different proteolytic enzymes in solution or FASP protocol does not significantly affect sequence coverage, and de novo sequencing is the most efficient way to identify posttranslational modifications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of shotgun proteomic experiments on five model proteins.

the analysis of shotgun data on model proteins, which allowed us to determine the degree of sequence coverage in the methods of data processing using different search engines and de Novo sequencing software.
the development of methods for shotgun proteomic data treatment and the identification of protein sequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the search engines and the de novo sequencing software give comparable results, and the use of the FASP protocol is not recommended.
the use of different methods and software is a necessary condition for the identification of the maximum number of peptides in the sample.
the search engine and the de novo sequencing software are equally effective, but the latter is more time-consuming.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of different enzymes for hydrolysis of proteins, as well as the application of different data processing methods, does not significantly increase the sequence coverage of the model proteins.
the use of a single protease (trypsin) in the FASP method is the best choice for the shotgun proteomic data processing.
the use of different protease enzymes and the FASP protocol did not improve the sequence coverage, but the use of de novo software for data analysis did.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of different methods of data analysis and different proteases for hydrolysis of model proteins in solution and in FASP protocol allows to increase the sequence coverage of the analyzed proteins.

the use of multiprotease hydrolysates in shotgun proteomic data analyses allows one to obtain more complete sequence coverage of proteins, especially in the presence of post-translational modifications, and also to identify mutations in proteins.
the use of a multiprotease approach is an effective way to improve the sequence coverage of proteins.
